newsitem.title: USA: Missouri winter wheat crop 25 percent harvested.
newsitem.headline: Missouri winter wheat crop 25 percent harvested.

text.p: Missouri's winter wheat crop was 25 percent harvested as of Sunday, trailing the average of 32 percent, according to the state's agricultural statistics service weekly report.
Winter wheat condition was rated seven percent poor, 20 percent fair, 58 percent good and 15 percent excellent, an improvement on the the previous week.

Four percent of the corn crop was silking, behind 12 percent last year and six percent for the five-year average. The crop was rated three percent poor, 24 percent fair 60 percent good and 13 percent excellent.

Soybeans were 96 percent planted, a few days ahead of last year's 92 percent and the five-year average of 93 percent. Two percent were blooming, against none last year and two percent normally. The crop was rated six percent poor, 28 percent fair, 58 percent good and eight percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated one percent very short, 13 percent short, 74 percent adequate and 12 percent surplus.
Pastures and ranges were rated one percent very poor, nine percent poor, 31 percent fair, 52 percent good and seven percent excellent.
